headline: Heard an appeal over which side of a fence at 485 South Union Street faces outward.
summary: Alexander Garlick appealed an administrative decision on permit ZPF-24-63. He said he disputes where the fence posts are placed, not which side is finished. The hearing closed so members could deliberate.

BURLINGTON DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD

MINUTES 
 
 Hybrid & In Person (at 645 Pine Street) Meeting 
 
Board Members Present: Caitlin Halpert, Evan Gould, Geoff Hand, Sean McKenzie, Miles Waite, Chase 
Taylor, and Marina Loughlin 
 
Board Members Absent: None 
 
Staff Members Present: Mary O’Neil, Matthew Clark, and Joseph Cava 
 
Staff Members Absent: Scott Gustin and Kirk Dressing 
 
I. Agenda 
II. Communications 
III. Minutes 
IV. Public Hearing 
 
1. ZAP-26-14; 485 South Union Street (RM, Ward 6) Elise Tarbi / Alexander Garlick   
Appeal of administrative decision of ZPF-24-63 for which side of the fence is finished for permit 
closure. (Project Manager, Matthew Clark) 
Elise Tarbi, owner, present, Alexander Garlick: Sworn in.  
 
Evan Gould: This is an appeal of an administrative decision. Is the appellant present? 
 
Alexander Garlick: Yes. 
 
Evan Gould: In the case of appeals, we will hear the facts of the case from City staff, then open it up 
for the appellant to speak. Can you tell us about the facts of this case and decision? 
 
Matthew Clark: This is in regards to ZPF-24-63. As it stands, the first permit condition presents 
language of the orientation on the finished side of the fence. The unfinished side of the fence is 
facing outward towards the abutting properties. This is not a repair of an existing fence, but the 
installation of a new style of fence. The photos of what previously existed do not match what was 
installed.   
 
Sean McKenzie: Where are the pictures taken from? 
 
Alexander Garlick: The opposite site of the property line facing outwards. 
 
Geoff Hand: The old fence appears to be a picket style fence, while the new installation appears to 
be a stockade fence.
Caitlin Halpert: I have a question on whether this fence is in kind or not. From the project plans, it 
appears the completed fence matches what was included with the approved project plans.  
 
Matthew Clark: Correct, but from my interpretation of this because the style of fence has changed 
this is what required a permit.  
 
Geoff Hand: But if they have a permit for the work the appeal is based off of which orientation the 
finished side is facing. The type of fencing installed matches the approved plans, it just was not 
installed right.  
 
Evan Gould: Are there any additional questions or comments from members of the Board? Hearing 
none, we will now open it up to the appellant to speak.  
 
Alexander Garlick: I think you are all caught up to the details on the facts of the case. The submitted 
photographs are from when we first purchased the property in 2022. It was overgrown for a portion 
of time and was blown over by the wind. We eventually found a contractor willing to work in 
Burlington who completed the work in fall 2024. I consulted with my neighbors about a replacement 
fence. I am not disputing the finished versus unfinished side, but the location of the posts that 
determine which way the fence is facing. It was a communication with the Zoning Division that led 
to this issue. Unfortunately, the contractor finished the project, so I have no way to undo what was 
already completed. That is my narrative and I raised a technical point in my appeal. Afterwards, the 
Zoning Division informed me  
 
Evan Gould: The previous fence was a stockade fence.  
 
Alexander Garlick: What is a stockade fence? 
 
Miles Waite: A fence composed of vertical slats, tightly grouped.  
 
Caitlin Halpert: A zoning permit was required for the visual change in fence type.  
 
Alexander Garlick: I did not know emailing through the online OpenGov permitting portal, but a 
privacy fence is described as something that cannot be seen through.  
 
Evan Gould: Are there any additional questions or comments from the Board? 
 
Sean McKenzie: Do you know the difference between a stockade fence and a picket fence? 
 
Alexander Garlick: Yes. 
 
Evan Gould: Are there any questions or comments from members of the public attending in person 
or online? Hearing none, we will close the hearing on this item to deliberate on it. 
 
V. Adjournment 
Hearing closed at 5:35 PM. 
 
 
 
Participation in the DRB proceeding is a prerequisite to the right to take any subsequent appeal.  Please note that ANYTHING
